newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Austria's BBAG 1996 pretax surges 69 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Austria's BBAG 1996 pretax surges 69 percent.

text.p: Austria's top drinks group BBAG said on Wednesday its final 1996 pre-tax profit jumped 69 percent to 1.304 billion schillings ($108.9 million), boosted by the sale of its Coca-Cola franchises in Poland and Austria.
Net profit rose to 1.085 billion against 627 million a year ago, while turnover eased to 10.17 billion schillings, compared with 11.08 billion in 1995.
"It was not an easy year but we have achieved a very good result," chief executive Johannes Brandl of Oesterreichische Brau-Beteiligungs AG (BBAG) told a news conference.
Beer sales inched up to 8.38 billion schillings against 8.37 billion last year, while soft drink sales dropped 72 percent to 1.26 billion schillings.
Brandl said the group would pay a 1996 dividend of 19 schillings, including a three schillings bonus payment, from 17 schillings last year.
Finance Director Walther Sachs told Reuters the basic dividend would remain at the same level next year but the company was unlikely to pay another three schilling bonus.
"The three schillings bonus was solely to give shareholders some of the spoils of the Cola disposal," he said.
BBAG unit Brau Union AG will pay an unchanged dividend for 1996 of 23 schillings, BBAG said. Brau Union controls about two thirds of the Austrian beer market.
Brandl predicted BBAG's pre-tax profit in 1997 would remain below one billion schillings, but roughly at the same level as 1996 discounting the Coca-Cola sell-off.
"One billion schillings pre-tax (for 1997) is out of the question," he noted.
In the first quarter BBAG had seen mild growth in beer sales and stronger growth in alcohol-free drinks, he added.
"In terms of results we are doing well in the first quarter but the summer can change the picture completely," said Brandl.

While the European beer market declined 1.7 percent in 1996, BBAG's beer exports rose 2.5 percent, with strong growth in former Soviet states. Exports remained key to the company's growth strategy, it said.
Group beer sales overall fell 1.6 percent to 8.17 million hectoclitres, while overall soft drink sales slipped to 1.35 million hectolitres from 2.69 million while fruit drinks sales rose 13 percent.
Brandl said the group's main target area remained Central Europe, particularly Romania, where it hopes to improve its market share to 10 percent from three percent at present.
BBAG owns Hungarian breweries Sopron and Martfu, Starobrno in the Czech Republic and Arbema in Romania.

The Association of Austrian Analysts said on Wednesday BBAG earnings per share rose to 47 schillings in 1996 from 44 schillings in 1995. Brau Union earnings per share climbed to 56 schillings from 48 schillings a year earlier.
BBAG's shares rose five schillings to close at 710, while Brau Union was up 12 schillings at 701.00 in an overall strong Vienna market. ($ = 11.96 Austrian Schillings)
